newsitem.title: GERMANY: Henkel declines comment on Loctite talk.
newsitem.headline: Henkel declines comment on Loctite talk.

text.p: German chemicals group Henkel KGaA on Wednesday declined to comment on news U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp held talks with another group, possibly find a white knight to fend off Henkel's takeover bid.

But analysts, all speaking on the condition they remain anonymous, said Henkel will likely respond by raising its offer, emerging the winner in the hostile takeover battle, as it already owns a 35 percent stake in Loctite.

When asked to comment on news that Loctite met with a potential rival to Henkel, Wolfgang Beynio, a senior Henkel official said, "We do not want to make any comment on any of these questions at this time."
"We will comment on this issue at the appropriate time," he added.
Henkel, fresh from acquiring German haircare products group Hans Schwarzkopf GmbH from Hoechst AG last year, has made a $57.75 a-share tender offer for the 65 percent of Loctite it does not own.
Loctite would complement Henkel's activities by increasing the German group's geographic presence and giving its access to products producing high margins.
Analysts said Loctite is a key prize for Henkel which is eager to further shore up its business after suffering during the European recession.

And to get Loctite, one analyst said, "I think they will be willing to raise their bid somewhere to the low 60 dollar level." Henkel's current offer is already a shade higher than its first $56 offer, and the group has until January 6 to possibly raise its bid. Loctite shares last traded at 60-1/8.
One analyst even questioned whether there is a white knight and whether Loctite is not just holding talks to force Henkel to raise its bid.

"It would be extremely difficult for a white knight to come in and run the group since Henkel already owns 35 percent, and I wonder whether there actually is a white knight and if Loctite is not just using this to help prop up the price," the analyst said.
